user.title: HAAC Bridge
user.description: Adds HAAC Bridge, which gives the HA Android Client a filtered view of your entities. After adding it, choose which users may see which entities under the options of the integration.

init.title: Users of the app
init.description: Choose which Home Assistant users the HA Android Client may show entities to. Users configured in configuration.yaml are not listed here and keep their YAML settings.

logging.title: Logging
logging.description: The log level decides what the bridge writes to the Home Assistant log: `warning` shows problems only, `info` also records every switching action of the app and of schedules, `debug` adds every request. Values set in the `logging` block of configuration.yaml win; set there: {yaml}.

data.activity: Show switching actions on the Activity page

remove_user.title: Remove a user
remove_user.description: The app will show this user no entities, and the user's schedules are deleted.

confirm_remove.title: Remove this user?
confirm_remove.description: {user} has {count} schedule(s) in the app. They are deleted together with the user's entry, and their entities disappear from Home Assistant. Submit to remove the user.

filter.title: What may this user see?
filter.description: Only switches, sensors, binary sensors and climate devices are ever shown. Binary sensors can show who is home or whether a door is open, so include single entities rather than the whole domain. Include at least one domain, entity or wildcard. An exclusion always wins over an inclusion. Wildcards look like `sensor.*_humidity`.

export_yaml.title: Export as YAML
export_yaml.description:
These are the users configured here. Copy the text into the import of another installation, or into configuration.yaml (restart or reload is needed there).

```yaml
{yaml}
```

import_yaml.title: Import from YAML
import_yaml.description: Paste a `haac_bridge:` section or just its content. Users are named by `user_id`. A user in the text replaces that user's entry here; other users stay as they are.

names.title: Names in the app
names.description: Optional names for the entities you included one by one. Leave a field empty to keep the Home Assistant name.

error.no_include: Choose at least one domain, entity or wildcard to include
error.invalid_glob: A wildcard must look like `domain.pattern`, for example `sensor.*_humidity`
error.invalid_config: The YAML does not match the haac_bridge configuration
error.needs_user_id: Name each user by user_id; a username cannot be imported
error.unknown_user: A user_id does not belong to an active Home Assistant user

cfg_invalid.title: HAAC Bridge configuration is invalid (HAB-CFG-001)
cfg_invalid.description: The haac_bridge section in configuration.yaml could not be loaded, so the previous configuration stays active. Check the Home Assistant log for details, fix the configuration and run the action `haac_bridge.reload`.

cfg_unknown_user.title: HAAC Bridge user not found (HAB-CFG-002)
cfg_unknown_user.description: The haac_bridge configuration refers to the user `{user}`, which does not exist in Home Assistant. This entry exposes nothing. Correct the `username` or `user_id` and run the action `haac_bridge.reload`.

sch_unreadable.title: HAAC Bridge cannot read stored schedules ({code})
sch_unreadable.description: {count} stored schedule(s) could not be read. They are kept unchanged in the storage file and are not run or shown in the app. Restore a backup of `.storage/haac_bridge.schedules` or update HAAC Bridge, then restart Home Assistant. The log names the error for each entry.

cfg_duplicate_user.title: HAAC Bridge user configured twice (HAB-CFG-003)
cfg_duplicate_user.description: {count} entries in the haac_bridge section of configuration.yaml refer to the user `{user}` (by `username` or `user_id`). Only the first entry is used. Remove or merge the others and run the action `haac_bridge.reload`.

reload.name: Reload
reload.description: Reloads the haac_bridge configuration from configuration.yaml.
